    \ge\frac1{(s-u)^2}\ge\frac1{s^2},
  \]
  and hence $\Lambda_n''(u)\le-1/(n+1)^2$ for every integer $n\ge4$ and every $u\in[0,1]$.

  First suppose $n=4$.
  The function $u\mapsto\Lambda_4(u)-(1-u)/70$ is concave on $[12/13,1]$, so it suffices to prove that both endpoint values exceed $1/4000$.
  Using $\log(1+u)\le Q(u)$, $Q(1/4)=25/112$, $\widehat z_5(12/13)=3849/17225$, and $\widehat z_5(1)=99/400$, we obtain
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      \Lambda_4(12/13)-\frac{1-12/13}{70}
       & >\frac{92}{455}-Q\left(\frac{3849}{17225}\right) \\
       & >\frac{92}{455}-\frac{21}{104}
      =\frac1{3640}>\frac1{4000},                         \\
      \Lambda_4(1)
       & >\frac{149}{672}-Q\left(\frac{99}{400}\right)    \\
       & >\frac{149}{672}-\frac{31}{140}
      =\frac1{3360}>\frac1{4000}.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  The bounds $Q(3849/17225)<21/104$ and $Q(99/400)<31/140$ follow by substituting into $Q(u)=u(6+u)/(6+4u)$.
  Concavity therefore implies $\Lambda_4(u)-(1-u)/70>1/4000$ for every $u\in[12/13,1]$.
  In particular, $\Lambda_4(a)-(1-a)/70>1/4000$ because $a\in(12/13,1)$.

  Now suppose $n\ge5$.
  Since $\Lambda_n''(u)\le-1/(n+1)^2$ for every $u\in[0,1]$, the function $u\mapsto\Lambda_n(u)-u(1-u)/(2(n+1)^2)$ is concave on $[0,1]$.
  Applying concavity at $u=a$ between the endpoints $0$ and $1$, we obtain
  \[
    \Lambda_n(a)
    \ge a\Lambda_n(1)
    +(1-a)\left[\Lambda_n(0)+\frac{a}{2(n+1)^2}\right].
  \]
  Applying $\log(1+u)\le Q(u)$ with $u=1/n$, we obtain
  \[
    \Lambda_n(0)
    >1-nQ(1/n)-\frac1{2n}
    =-\frac1{n(3n+2)}.
  \]
  Since $a\ge12/13$, we have
  \[
    \Lambda_n(0)+\frac{a}{2(n+1)^2}
    >\frac{5n^2-14n-13}{13n(3n+2)(n+1)^2}>0,
  \]
  where $5n^2-14n-13=5(n-4)^2+26(n-4)+11>0$ for $n\ge4$.
  Hence, $\Lambda_n(a)\ge a\Lambda_n(1)$.
  At $u=1$, we have $\widehat z_{n+1}(1)=(19n+23)/(20n(n+1))$.
  Applying $\log(1+u)\le Q(u)$ to both logarithms in the definition of $\Lambda_n$ gives
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      \Lambda_n(1)
       & >1+\frac{11}{24n}-nQ(1/n)
      -Q\left(\frac{19n+23}{20n(n+1)}\right)               \\
       & =\frac3{6n+4}+\frac{11}{24n}
      -Q\left(\frac{19n+23}{20n(n+1)}\right)               \\
       & =\frac{n^2\{180(n-5)^2+621(n-5)+553\}+5145n+1886}
      {240n(n+1)(3n+2)(30n^2+49n+23)}
      >\frac1{100n^3}.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  For the last inequality, the numerator exceeds $500n^2$ for $n\ge5$, while the denominator is less than $50000n^5$.
  Here we use $n+1<5n/4$, $3n+2<7n/2$, and $30n^2+49n+23<42n^2$.
  It follows that
  \[
    \Lambda_n(a)>\frac{a}{100n^3}>\frac1{500n^3}.
  \]

  Comparing $\Lambda_4(a)-(1-a)/70>1/4000$ for $n=4$ and $\Lambda_n(a)>1/(500n^3)$ for $n\ge5$ with \eqref{eq:node-short-tail}, we obtain, for every integer $n$ with $4\le n\le k-2$,
  \[
    \log\frac{H_n}{p_0(1+\widehat z_{n+1}(a))}>\frac{T_n}{p_0}\ge0.
  \]
  Exponentiating and using $\exp(u)\ge1+u$ for $u\ge0$ and $\widehat z_s(a)>0$, we obtain
  \[
    z_s=\frac{H_n}{p_0}-\frac{T_n}{p_0}-1
    >\widehat z_s(a)\left(1+\frac{T_n}{p_0}\right)
    \ge\widehat z_s(a).
  \]
  This proves \eqref{eq:node-unified-denominator}.

  It remains to consider $s=k$.
  Here $q=(k-1)/k$, and $\mathbb{E}(N-k+1)_+=0$ because $N\le k-1$.
  Using the binomial distribution of $N$, we obtain
  \[
    1-V_k=\mathbb{E} q^{k-1-N}=(\delta+aq)^{k-1}=(1-x)^{k-1}.
  \]
  Equation \eqref{eq:node-energy-linear} implies $r_*(W_k)=M_*(W_k)=1$.
  Thus,
  \[
    r_*(W_k)-\frac{19M_*(W_k)}{20}
    =\frac1{20}>\frac{x}{5},
  \]
  since $x<1/k\le1/6<1/4$.
  Thus, $r_*(W_s)-19M_*(W_s)/20>x/5$ for every integer $s$ with $4\le s\le k$.

  Fix an arbitrary $t\in[W_4,W_k]$.
  Choose an integer $s\in\{4,\ldots,k-1\}$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$ such that $t=(1-\theta)W_s+\theta W_{s+1}$.
  On $[W_s,W_{s+1}]$, the functions $r_*$ and $a^k-V_*$ are affine, and $a^k-V_*>0$ by \ref{item:profile-positive}.
  The reciprocal of a positive affine function is convex, so $M_*$ is convex and $r_*-19M_*/20$ is concave on the same interval.
  Applying concavity and then the margin at $W_s$ and $W_{s+1}$, we obtain
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      r_*(t)-\frac{19M_*(t)}{20}
       & \ge(1-\theta)\left(r_*(W_s)-\frac{19M_*(W_s)}{20}\right)        \\
       & \quad+\theta\left(r_*(W_{s+1})-\frac{19M_*(W_{s+1})}{20}\right)
      >\frac{x}{5}.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  This proves \ref{item:profile-margin}.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
In \eqref{eq:large-defect-endpoint-functions}, write $s=\eta/a$ and $u=x_0/A$.
  Throughout, $(t,s,u)\in[0,1/6]\times[1/10,1]\times[0,1/3]$ and $\beta(s)=\sqrt{(1+s)/11}$.
  We have $\mathcal V_0(t,s,u)=s-1/20+13u/20+t(1-s)/6$ and $\mathcal V_1(t,s,u)=\mathcal V_0(t,s,u)+(1-s)/9$.

  We first prove $P_1>0$.
  For fixed $s,u$, the functions $Q_1$ and $R$ are nondecreasing in $t$, whereas
  \[
    \partial_t[(1-t)\mathcal V_1]
    =-\frac{19}{18}\left(s-\frac1{10}\right)
    -\frac{13u}{20}-\frac{t(1-s)}3\le0.
  \]
  Since $\beta(s)>0$, we have $P_1(t,s,u)\ge P_1(1/6,s,u)$.
  At $t=1/6$, we have
  \[
    \beta(s)\sqrt{\frac56\mathcal V_1(1/6,s,u)}
    =\sqrt{\frac{(1+s)(155s+16+117u)}{2376}}.
  \]
  Since $1+s$ and $155s+16+117u$ are positive and affine in $(s,u)$, concavity of $(r_1,r_2)\mapsto\sqrt{r_1r_2}$ on $(0,\infty)^2$ implies that $\beta(s)\sqrt{(5/6)\mathcal V_1(1/6,s,u)}$ is jointly concave in $(s,u)$.
  Moreover,
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      Q_1(1/6,s,u) & =\left(\frac{39s}{40}-\frac{11u}{24}-\frac18\right)_+, \\
      R(1/6,s,u)   & =\frac{\max\{u,(7-5s)/32\}}3
      +\frac{u+(7-5s)/32}{14}.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  Thus, $Q_1(1/6,s,u)$ and $R(1/6,s,u)$ are jointly convex, so $P_1(1/6,s,u)$ is jointly concave and
  \[
    P_1(t,s,u)\ge
    \min_{(s_0,u_0)\in\{1/10,1\}\times\{0,1/3\}}
    P_1(1/6,s_0,u_0).
  \]
  Substituting $(s,u)\in\{1/10,1\}\times\{0,1/3\}$ gives
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      P_1(1/6,1/10,0)
       & =\sqrt{\frac7{480}}-\frac{221}{2688}
      >\frac1{10}-\frac{221}{2688}
      =\frac{239}{13440}>0,                                      \\
      P_1(1/6,1/10,1/3)
       & =\sqrt{\frac{47}{1440}}-\frac{1205}{8064}
      >\frac16-\frac{1205}{8064}
      =\frac{139}{8064}>0,                                       \\
      P_1(1/6,1,0)
       & =\sqrt{\frac{19}{132}}-\frac{17}{50}-\frac{17}{672}
      >\frac38-\frac{17}{50}-\frac{17}{672}
      =\frac{163}{16800}>0,                                      \\
      P_1(1/6,1,1/3)
       & =\sqrt{\frac{35}{198}}-\frac{251}{900}-\frac{281}{2016}
      >\frac{21}{50}-\frac{251}{900}-\frac{281}{2016}
      =\frac{29}{16800}>0.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  Hence, $P_1>0$ on $[0,1/6]\times[1/10,1]\times[0,1/3]$.

  We now prove $P_0>0$.
  For fixed $t$, the function $\frac12\sqrt{(1-t)\mathcal V_0(t,s,u)}$ is jointly concave in $(s,u)$, whereas $Q_0$ and $R$ are jointly convex.
  Hence, $P_0$ is jointly concave in $(s,u)$, so
  \[
    P_0(t,s,u)\ge
    \min_{(s_0,u_0)\in\{1/10,1\}\times\{0,1/3\}}
    P_0(t,s_0,u_0).
  \]
  At $s=1$, we have $\mathcal V_0=\mathcal V_1$, $Q_0-Q_1=3/20$, $(1-t)\mathcal V_1\ge19/24$, and $\beta(1)=\sqrt{2/11}<3/7$.
  Therefore,
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      P_0(t,1,u)-P_1(t,1,u)
       & >\frac1{14}\sqrt{\frac{19}{24}}-\frac3{50} \\
       & >\frac1{14}\cdot\frac89-\frac3{50}
      =\frac{11}{3150}>0.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  Since $P_1>0$, we obtain $P_0(t,1,u)>0$.
  At $(s,u)=(1/10,1/3)$, we have $Q_0=0$, $E\le13/64$, and $(1-t)\mathcal V_0\ge(5/6)(4/15)=2/9$, so
  \[
    P_0(t,1/10,1/3)>
    \frac16-\frac19-\frac{1/3+13/64}{14}
    =\frac{139}{8064}>0.
  \]
  Finally, at $(s,u)=(1/10,0)$, we have $Q_0=1/10$, $R=17(2+27t)/1344$, and $(1-t)\mathcal V_0=(1-t)(1+3t)/20$.
  The function $t\mapsto(1-t)(1+3t)/20$ is positive and concave on $[0,1/6]$, so $t\mapsto P_0(t,1/10,0)$ is concave.
  At $t=0$ and $t=1/6$, we have
  \[
    \begin{aligned}
      P_0(0,1/10,0)   & >\frac1{10}-\frac1{25}-\frac{17}{672}>0, \\
      P_0(1/6,1/10,0) & =\frac{187}{67200}>0.
    \end{aligned}
  \]
  Thus, $P_0>0$ on $[0,1/6]\times[1/10,1]\times[0,1/3]$.
